messages:
Maya: Hi folks - quick question. I'm exploring IVF treatment next month and the clinic asked if our Redwood plan requires pre-authorization and if there are any lifetime limits or specific coverage rules. I'm going through an OBGYN referral but want to understand what docs I should gather so the claim and prior auth go smoothly.

Alex (People Ops): Congrats on taking the step, Maya. Short answer: yes, fertility services often need pre-authorization and have specific coverage rules depending on plan tier. Steps to start: 1) Confirm whether your chosen clinic/provider is in-network for fertility services (search via the carrier provider directory). 2) Ask the clinic to submit a prior authorization (PA) with CPT codes for the planned procedures (e.g., 58970, 58974, 58976, 58951 depending on the service). 3) We'll need a medical necessity letter from the reproductive endocrinologist outlining diagnosis, recommended procedures, dates, and estimated cycles.

Maya: Any idea about lifetime cycle caps or required documentation like prior unsuccessful treatments? The clinic said some insurers want documentation of infertility duration.

Priya: Good question. Our Redwood medical plan (PPO) follows the carrier's clinical policy. Common requirements: documentation of infertility (usually 12 months unprotected intercourse OR 6 months for women over 35), prior conservative therapy if applicable, and a clear treatment plan. Some plans have a cap on number of covered cycles or a lifetime dollar cap; others cover specific services (diagnostics, retrieval, embryo transfer) but limit IVF medications or lab fees. We can check your specific plan and confirm limits.

Alex (People Ops): To make this fast, upload: clinic pre-auth request (if they already started), medical necessity letter, proposed CPT list, and any prior EHR notes showing infertility workup. Use subject line "IVF PA request - [Your Name]" when emailing benefits@redwood.com or upload via the portal.

Maya: If the clinic is out-of-network, do we handle pre-auth differently? They're a specialist clinic but out-of-network for my region.

Priya: If OON, the carrier still accepts prior auth requests but reimbursement will follow OON rules (higher member cost share). For high-cost care, sometimes carriers will approve in-network benefits when there's a demonstrated lack of reasonable in-network providers; that's an exception review (you'll need a statement that you tried X in-network clinics and why they were unsuitable). We can help escalate if you want us to try an exception.

Maya: Timeline-wise, how long for PA decisions? I need to schedule retrieval windows.

Alex (People Ops): Typical PA turnaround is 7-14 business days once the carrier has complete docs. If the clinic marks it as urgent (time-sensitive window), it can be faster. When you send to benefits, put the intended treatment date range and ask the clinic to mark the request as urgent. We'll track it and follow up proactively.

Maya: Anything else I should sign or authorize? HIPAA release?

Priya: Yes — if you want us to speak to the clinic or the carrier on your behalf, sign the simple release form we'll email. Also, if the carrier asks for additional records, we'll coordinate with you on secure upload.

BenefitsBot: Helpful links: Benefits portal PA upload: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/pa-upload ; fertility policy summary: https://benefits.redwood.com/policies/fertility-summary (check "Plan-specific limits" section). For secure docs use: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload.

Maya: Awesome, uploading the clinic PA packet and medical necessity letter now. Thanks for the clarity! :heart:
